summary: Carter Dome summit lookout: watch tower by 1915 under the Forest Service, steel cab added 1924, destroyed 1947; footings remain beside the AT.

facts.status_note: Abandoned and destroyed in 1947; footings and an anchor remain on the summit, per photo captions.
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (from 1915; New Hampshire Forestry Commission before)

access.note: The Appalachian Trail runs over the summit, so hikers reach it on foot.

visit.trail_note: Hike the Appalachian Trail over the summit; the footings are on the summit.

events.note: Observation towers built by local woodsmen and guides, per Willhite Web
New and improved watch tower; the USFS took control from the NH Forestry Commission
New trail to the summit, opening the way for a telephone line and observation quarters
New steel tower with a cab, described as 30 feet

evidence.supports: observation towers built by local woodsmen and guides as early as 1876
evidence.quote: As early as 1876, observation towers were built by local woodsmen and guides.
In 1907, the location was used for fire observation.

evidence.supports: 1915 watch tower; USFS took over from the state Forestry Commission
evidence.quote: In 1915, a new and improved watch tower was constructed and the USFS took control from the NH Forestry Commission.
1915-16 biennium: A new and improved watch tower was constructed.

evidence.supports: 1922 trail to the top opened the way for a telephone line and observation quarters
evidence.quote: A new trail on a much improved location, constructed in 1922 to the top of Carter Dome, has opened the way for the construction of a new telephone line and observation quarters on this mountain

evidence.supports: 1922 report: day and night service in dry spells
evidence.quote: promise to give dependable day and night service during dry periods when the situation may require continuous vigilance
In 1924, a new 30 foot steel tower was cab was built.
In 1947, the tower was abandoned and destroyed.
Today the summit is wooded so no views.

evidence.supports: few spots to push through trees for a view north
evidence.quote: There are a few spots to push through some trees and get a photo or two of a view northward.

evidence.supports: footings and an anchor on the summit (photo captions)
evidence.quote: Summit and footings. White blaze on an anchor.
AT Access: Trail over the summit

evidence.supports: 1922 passage is from the Forestry Commission biennial report, 1921-22
evidence.quote: Biennial Report of the Forestry Commission, 1921-22

corrections.proposed: U.S. Forest Service (from 1915; New Hampshire Forestry Commission before)
corrections.why: The current value is a fragment of a date line from the Forest Lookouts page, not an agency. Willhite Web says the USFS took control from the NH Forestry Commission in 1915.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts dates the new watch tower to the 1915-16 biennium and Willhite Web to 1915. Both describe the same build, so the story uses 1915.

notes_for_editor: Built and fate rest on Willhite Web, a personal Appalachian Trail site, plus the Forest Lookouts page quoting the 1922 Forestry Commission report. The 1876 and 1907 dates appear only on Willhite Web. Staffing is not stated in any fetched source; a search snippet naming a 1928 keeper and a 1930 cabin caption were not verified on a page we could open, so they are left out. The record's agency field held a date fragment and is corrected. Do not confuse with us-nh-carter (the stone Carter Tower in Jefferson). The Wikipedia article for Carter Dome has no tower history. The firelookout.org Carter Dome page cited by a search returned 404, and the NHDFL history PDF returned 403, so neither was used. The '30 foot steel tower' wording is ambiguous; height_m 9.1 reads it as a 30-foot tower.
